brief: Morgan Stanley's 2027 US outlook: AI-related capex stays intact despite political risk from the midterms, anchoring spending by upper-income households through wealth effects, so growth holds at 2.5% in 2027 and 2.7% in 2028. Because most hyperscaler equipment is imported, AI investment adds to GDP via construction and services but leaks into imports, limiting domestic overheating; net trade still drags growth about 0.6pp as imports outpace exports. The labor market stays low-hire/low-fire (breakeven ~50k/month payrolls), with AI responsible for at most 15bp of the unemployment rate, concentrated among young workers. Disinflation is reluctant: tariff payback and slower airfare inflation pull core PCE down, offset by energy pass-through and healthcare costs, leaving core PCE at 2.6% in 2027. Because the estimated neutral rate has risen to about 150bp, the Fed hikes twice more to 4.25-4.5% by March 2027 before cutting to 3.5-3.75% in 2028. Fiscal deficits hold near 6% of GDP as the OBBBA's boost fades to neutral. Four alternative scenarios (45% base case) cover demand-driven overheating, a productivity upside, an oil/rate shock, and an AI spending slowdown.
